modules.description: A virtual machine on a local libvirt/QEMU host: provision a batch, tear one down, resize it, or read the inventory. Speaks the `wb-cloud` vm contract so an unmodified cloud scenario runs against a workstation.
modules.name: vm

created.description:
Provision `count` VMs and wait until every one of them is ready.
Idempotent on the batch identity: a rerun adopts the domains it already
made (matched by the domain metadata label `soulstack-run`, or by the
name `<name>-<seq>`) and tops up only what is missing, at the first free
indexes.
Each VM boots from a qcow2 overlay on the profile's image and a NoCloud
seed carrying `userdata`; ready means the guest took a DHCP lease and
reported a hostname, which is where sid and primary_ip come from.
Output.hosts is the provisioned batch, one entry per VM:
{sid, vm_id, primary_ip, external_ip, attributes}. It does NOT carry
bootstrap_token — minting one needs the Keeper's token store, which a
plugin has no access to, exactly as in the cloud artifact.
No dry-run preview.

ca_cert_pem.description: Accepted and unused: TLS to a remote libvirt is configured in libvirt's own client files, not here. Declared because the cloud contract declares it.

client_key_pem.description: Accepted and unused (see ca_cert_pem). Declared secret so it never reaches events or errors.

count.description: How many VMs the batch holds. The scan counts what already exists, so this is the TOTAL, not the number to add.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system. This is the one connection param that carries a local meaning: it is where the hypervisor lives, as the cloud endpoint is where the compute API lives.

key_id.description: Accepted and unused: a local libvirtd authenticates by socket permissions, not an API key. Declared because the cloud contract declares it.

name.description: Batch identity: domains are named `<name>-<seq>` and labelled with it. Required unless profile.labels["soulstack-run"] is set — without one of the two a rerun cannot recognise its own domains and would spawn orphans.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. One of namespace / namespace_id is required.

profile.description: The VM spec, same field names as the cloud artifact: namespace XOR namespace_id, network_id (UUID of a libvirt network), cpu_size (cores), ram_size and boot_disk_size (BYTES), rm_external_id (accepted and recorded; inert here), and the image as EITHER image_id (exact UUID, derived from the volume name) OR image_name (a volume in the image pool, e.g. debian-12). Plus the optional boot_disk_name / deletion_protection / labels. set_external_ip, external_ip_id, anti_affinity and cluster are REFUSED — see the README for why a silent no-op would be worse.

secret.description: Accepted and unused (see key_id). Still declared secret so that a stand which does put a real credential here never has it logged.

userdata.description: cloud-init user-data, at most 32 KiB. The cap is the cloud artifact's, mirrored deliberately: a seed ISO would hold more, and accepting more here would green a scenario that the cloud then refuses.

destroyed.description:
Delete every VM in `vm_ids` and CONFIRM the teardown by polling.
A domain that is still being defined can refuse to go; the delete is
re-issued until the domain and its volumes are gone. A teardown that
could not be confirmed is reported failed, with the vm_id, never as
success. A domain carrying deletion_protection is refused.
No dry-run preview.

vm_ids.description: Domain UUIDs to tear down. A VM that is already gone is an idempotent success.

probed.description:
Read the VM inventory of a namespace. Read-only, changed=false by
design (a probe, not a mutation): it creates, deletes and modifies
nothing. Only domains this artifact made are reported — the namespace
label is the scope, so an unrelated VM on the same workstation is
invisible here and untouchable by `destroyed`. Output.hosts has the same
shape `created` produces.
No dry-run preview.

run_label.description: Report only VMs carrying this value in the domain metadata label `soulstack-run` — the batch identity `created` stamps. Ignored when vm_ids is set.

secret.description: Accepted and unused (see key_id). Still declared secret so that a stand which does put a real credential here never has it logged.

vm_ids.description: Report only these domain UUIDs. Omitted, the whole namespace is listed (optionally narrowed by run_label).

resized.description:
Resize every VM in `vm_ids` to an ABSOLUTE target.
Disk grows online through a block resize (never shrinks — a target at or
below the current size is an idempotent skip); the guest filesystem
follows only if it runs growpart, exactly as in the cloud. cpu/ram go
through stop → update → start and therefore need allow_downtime. libvirt
could hot-plug some of that, and this does not: a local run that passed
without allow_downtime would red in the cloud.
The host's free memory and the disk pool's free space are prechecked
against the batch's summed positive delta: it fails closed, before any
VM is touched.
No dry-run preview.

allow_downtime.description: EXPLICIT consent to stop and start the VM. Required for a cpu/ram change and refused up front without it, so a batch never ends up half-stopped. A disk-only resize is online and does not need it.

ca_cert_pem.description: Accepted and unused: TLS to a remote libvirt is configured in libvirt's own client files, not here. Declared because the cloud contract declares it.

client_key_pem.description: Accepted and unused (see ca_cert_pem). Declared secret so it never reaches events or errors.

cpu_cores.description: Target vCPU count. 0 leaves cpu alone.

disk_gb.description: Target boot-disk size in GiB. 0 leaves the disk alone. Shrinking is refused as an idempotent skip.

endpoint.description: libvirt connection URI — e.g. qemu:///system. This is the one connection param that carries a local meaning: it is where the hypervisor lives, as the cloud endpoint is where the compute API lives.

key_id.description: Accepted and unused: a local libvirtd authenticates by socket permissions, not an API key. Declared because the cloud contract declares it.

namespace.description: Scope label stamped into domain metadata. It is what keeps this artifact away from VMs it did not create: `probed` and `destroyed` see nothing outside it. One of namespace / namespace_id is required.

ram_mb.description: Target RAM in MiB. 0 leaves ram alone.

secret.description: Accepted and unused (see key_id). Still declared secret so that a stand which does put a real credential here never has it logged.

vm_ids.description: Domain UUIDs to resize. Every VM in the batch gets the same target.
